registered: 2026-10-23T14:10-04:00 (before any run; the corpus generator scripts/corpus.py in openIE-dev/rce was written alongside this file and had not been run over the population when this was committed)
question: RCE-JEPA H1: is Form space much smaller than source space for the same programs? rho = b(code) / b(P), where b(P) is the bits to encode the Form canonically and b(code) the bits of the equivalent emitted source. The page states: supported if the median rho over the corpus is at least 5, disproved if below 2.
unit: one program = one row of results/forms.jsonl: path, licence, shape hash, intent block, nameless canonical source, verdict, sizes per target, rho per target, split
population: every .rce of openIE-dev/rce (main, commit recorded in the rows) under spec/examples, spec/examples-0.9/ok, programs, apps, book/listings (not under a refused/ directory), stdlib/lib, and the conformance tests whose expectation is accept, that rce check accepts standalone; multi-file packages are excluded, decided by rule before running

operationalisation.b_P: tokens(N) x log2 |V_P| where N is the nameless canonical source of the program (rce fmt --nameless: every declared identifier replaced by its positional name, so the measure does not reward or punish naming) and V_P is the set of distinct tokens over all N in the population
operationalisation.b_code: tokens(C_t) x log2 |V_t| where C_t is the program part of rce emit t (the emitted file minus the shared runtime prelude, which is the same bytes for every program and is checked to be a verbatim prefix) for t in python (primary), rust, js, scala, and V_t is the set of distinct tokens over all C_t in the population
operationalisation.tokenizer: one fixed regular expression for both sides: identifiers [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*, numbers, double- and single-quoted strings with escapes as one token each, every other non-space character as one token; full-line and trailing comments (# in RCE, // in the emitted languages, outside strings) are removed on both sides before tokenising
operationalisation.secondary_views: the same ratio with b = UTF-8 bytes x 8 (uncompressed) and with b = gzip -9 bytes x 8 (a compressed description length), reported next to the primary so a reader can see how much the vocabulary term matters
operationalisation.primary_metric: median rho over the population with t = python, and its interquartile range; the medians for rust, js and scala are secondary
operationalisation.near_duplicates: rows with the same shape hash (SHA-256 of the nameless canonical source) are collapsed to one before any statistic; the split is by shape hash (SHA-256 mod 10: 0 to 7 train, 8 validation, 9 test), never by surface text

hypotheses.H1: median rho (python) >= 5 supports H1 of the RCE-JEPA page; median rho < 2 disproves it; between 2 and 5 the result is recorded as neither

known_biases: the emitted programs carry type annotations, explicit error handling and runtime calls that the Form expresses by declaration; this inflates b(code) and is the point of H1 as stated on the page (the Form is the compact object). A reader who wants a tighter comparison should use the gzip view, which removes repetition the vocabulary term does not. The runtime prelude is excluded from b(code) because it is shared by every program; including it would make rho grow without bound for small programs.
exclusions: programs rce check refuses standalone; multi-file packages; decided by rule before running
reporting: every row kept in results/forms.jsonl; negatives (conformance rejects with their diagnostic code, and checker-verified token mutants of the accepted programs under a fixed seed) in results/negatives.jsonl; the dataset card in CARD.md; Wilson 95% intervals where a share is reported; cpu_s per program; no energy claim

frozen_run.engine: openIE-dev/rce main after PR #6 (the commit is written in every row), rce built from spec/checker with cargo build --release
frozen_run.generator: scripts/corpus.py of the same commit; the run is a pure function of the checkout and the seed 0x5eed_c0de_0001

amendments.after: the v1 run (RESULTS.md, CARD.md); before any v2 run

adds.typed_mutants: in addition to the three whitespace-token mutants, five token-class mutation operators under the same seed, two mutants each per accepted program: rename (one identifier occurrence replaced by another identifier of the same file), operator (one binary operator swapped within its class: + - * /, < <= > >=, == !=, and or), literal (one integer literal changed by +1, or negated when it is 0; one string literal gets a character appended), guard (one line beginning with if, elif, requires, ensures or fail removed), type (one type name swapped: u64 i64, i64 u64, text bool, bool text, f64 i64)
adds.mutant_outcomes: for every mutant: refused with its first diagnostic code; or accepted, and then (a) same shape as the parent, (b) different shape and the same trace heads as the parent (an equivalent program under the examples' events), or (c) different shape and different trace heads: a behaviour change that the program's own example lines and checks did not catch
adds.intent_mutation_score: over programs with at least one example line and at least one mutant that parses: the share of behaviour-changing mutants (accepted or refused only by W-INT-1, the example-does-not-hold rule) that the example lines catch. Reported per program and as a median with Wilson intervals on the pooled share. This is a measurement of how well the intent block pins behaviour, which the RCE-JEPA page needs for RJ-F2 and H7 and which dim-r2 raised (unobservable intent). No threshold is registered; it is descriptive at v2.
adds.check_cost: check_s per program: wall seconds of rce check alone (cpu of the reference checker, release build), reported as median and interquartile range; est_j = check_s x 10 W, labelled estimate, no meter; this is the checker side of H2, whose model side is not measurable here
